text:
devon-solutions: Hey team — running a PoC with a regulated EU bank. They asked for a very concise artifact showing where customer data lands, which subprocessors touch it, and how keys are managed. Need something we can hand to their infosec by EOD Thu.

maria-sales: Can we reuse the standard dataflow + subproc table? They want explicit KMS info and any cross-region egress called out. 

devon-solutions: Prefer a one-page diagram + a single table listing subprocessors, region, purpose, and whether they have access to plaintext. Also call out any third-party telemetry/logging and retention windows.

ari-privacy: @devon-solutions quick clarifying Qs: Do they require customer-managed keys (CMK) or is KMS with HSM-backed keys OK? Any restrictions on abroad subprocessors (non-EU)?

devon-solutions: They prefer CMK but will accept provider KMS if keys are HSM-backed and we can provide key lifecycle notes. They explicitly asked to avoid US-based subprocessors touching plaintext.

sam-eng: For the hosted stack, typical flow is: customer request -> fronting LB (region) -> inference service (model host) -> optional dedicated cache layer -> logging/metrics pipeline. Only the logging pipeline sends traces to third-party analytics; logs can be configured to redact. We can pin model inference to eu-west-1 (Ireland) or eu-central-1 (Frankfurt).

jess-sre: Adding constraints: if we choose Frankfurt for both compute and storage, we can avoid cross-border egress except to our monitoring provider in the EU. We currently have an EU monitoring endpoint (Dataplane-EU) in Amsterdam that we can route logs to, which keeps data in EU.

ari-privacy: Draft checklist for their packet: 1) Region(s) used (FR/eu-central-1), 2) Subprocessor list with access type, 3) KMS type (CMK / HSM), 4) Logs & retention, 5) Network boundaries and any egress flows, 6) Export control notes.

devon-solutions: I sketched a minimal ASCII flow to be included — feel free to copy/paste.

devon-solutions: ```
Client -> TLS -> LB (eu-central-1) -> Inference Node (Pinned model v1.2, KV cache disabled for PII) -> Storage (encrypted-at-rest, customer-region) 
                  ↓
                Logging -> EU Monitoring Endpoint (Dataplane-EU)
KMS: HSM-backed keys, customer-specified CMK via KMS API (optional)
Subprocessors: See table below (all EU-based for this PoC)
```

maria-sales: This is great. Can you also add a short sentence that we can include in their vendor-risk doc: "Redwood Inference restricts all PoC compute and storage to the customer-selected EU region and supports customer-managed keys with HSM-backed KMS"?

ari-privacy: Wording tweak: add that audit logs are immutable and that key rotation is supported.

devon-solutions: OK. I'll put together: 1-pg diagram (SVG), 1-pg subproc table, 1-paragraph KMS + retention statement. ETA: 6 hours.

jess-sre: Ping @sec-bot for automated evidence pack (SOC/TLS certs + subproc list export).

sec-bot: Evidence pack created: soci-report-eu-2025.pdf, tls-certs-2026-02.zip, subproc-export-2026-03.csv (link: https://redwood.internal/artefacts/1854001111).

maria-sales: Friendly reminder — include contact for legal/DP questions (ari-privacy). I'll send the handoff email once we have the artifacts. :email:

devon-solutions: Thanks everyone. I'll post the two artifacts here when done and attach the ASCII + the subproc table. Anyone object to labeling this PoC "EU-only compute + CMK option"?

ari-privacy: No objections. Just ensure the table explicitly marks ANY non-EU subprocessors as not used for this PoC.

sam-eng: I'll validate the network egress rules and lock the infra config for the PoC (no outbound to US).

devon-solutions: Great. Closing loop — will drop files here in ~6h and update thread_ts if needed.

maria-sales: Perfect, thanks :thumbsup:
